mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying, exalted is He, {تِلْكَ آيَات الْكتاب}: تِلْكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and آيات is the khabar (predicate). It points to what had been revealed of the Qur'an. It is also said that rather it points to these letters at the openings of the surahs, because the verses of the Qur'an are composed of them. It is also said that تِلْكَ is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "these are those verses of the clear Book which you were promised in your scriptures", because they had been promised in the Torah and the Gospel that the Qur'an would be sent down.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {أَلا يَكُونُوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {وَإِذ نَادَى}: i.e. "and recite to them when He called".

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying أَن عبدت: أَن is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for نعْمَة. It may also be in the position of the accusative, on the implied form "because you enslaved" (لِأَن عبدت), after which the preposition was omitted; its omission with أَن is frequent in speech and in the Qur'an. For this reason some grammarians said that أَن is in the position of the genitive by the omitted preposition, because, since its omission with أَن is so frequent, it governs even though it is omitted.

mekki-muskil:77-77.t:
His saying {فَإِنَّهُم عَدو لي}: عَدو is a singular that stands for a group, so it is not made plural, and it comes for the feminine without the tāʾ marbūṭa (hāʾ): you say هِيَ عَدو الله. Al-Farrāʾ reported عدوة الله. Al-Akhfash the Younger said: whoever says عدوة with the hāʾ means "hostile (fem.)" (معادية), and whoever says عَدو without the hāʾ does not make it plural or dual; that is only by way of relation (nisba).
His saying {إِلَّا رب الْعَالمين}: accusative by the exception that is not of the same kind as the first, because they used to worship idols, and their acknowledgement of Allah together with their worship of idols did not benefit them. Al-Zajjāj allowed it to be of the same kind as the first, because they used to worship Allah alongside their idols.

mekki-muskil:149-149.t: His saying {فارهين}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in تنحتون.

mekki-muskil:176-176.t:
His saying {أَصْحَاب الأيكة}: whoever reads the tāʾ with fatḥa makes it the name of the town, and so does not inflect it fully (makes it a diptote) because of definiteness and femininity; its pattern is فعلة. Whoever reads the tāʾ in the genitive makes it definite by the alif and lām, and puts it in the genitive because أَصْحَاب is annexed to it. Its origin is أيكة, the name of a place with dense, intertwined trees and doum palms. Al-Mubarrad did not recognise ليكة on the pattern فعلة; in his view it is only أيكة with the two letters of definiteness added to it, so it is fully inflected, and the reading of whoever reads the tāʾ with fatḥa is in his view a mistake. The tāʾ can only be with kasra because of the annexation, and the lām is the lām of definiteness onto which the vowel of the hamza with fatḥa was thrown, so it took fatḥa, just as they said لحمر for الْأَحْمَر and سل for اسْأَل.
His saying {مَا أغْنى عَنْهُم}: مَا is interrogative, in the position of the accusative by أغنى. It may also be a particle of negation, and the second مَا is in the position of the nominative by أغنى. [Translator's note: {مَا أغْنى عَنْهُم} is at al-Shuʿarāʾ 207; the source places it under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:193-193.t: His saying {نزل بِهِ الرّوح الْأمين}: بِهِ may be in the position of the object of نزل, and بِهِ may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as you say "Zayd went out with his clothes", and of this kind is His saying, exalted is He, {وَقد دخلُوا بالْكفْر وهم قد خَرجُوا بِهِ}, i.e. they entered as disbelievers and went out as disbelievers. He did not mean that they entered with something they carried with them; He meant only that they entered in a state and went out in that same state.

mekki-muskil:209-209.t: His saying {ذكرى وَمَا كُنَّا}: the position of ذكرى according to al-Kisāʾī is the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Zajjāj said: as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of {إِلَّا لَهَا منذرون} is "reminding a reminder". ذكرى may also be in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "our warning is a reminder", or "that is a reminder", or "this is a reminder". It may be given tanwīn if you make it a maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:227-227.t: His saying {أَي مُنْقَلب يَنْقَلِبُون}: you make أيا accusative by ينقلبون, and it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar of ينقلبون, its implied form being "by what overturning they will be overturned" (أَي انقلاب يَنْقَلِبُون). It may not be made accusative by سيعلم, because the interrogative is not governed by what precedes it, since it has the head of the sentence (ṣadr al-kalām); only what comes after it governs it. It is also said that what precedes it does not govern it only because it (what precedes) is a statement (khabar), and a statement does not govern an interrogative, since the two are different.
